transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-21T16:00:00Z
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Lisa Harper (CISO, Bank of Riverbend), Tom Delaney (Head of Engineering), Priya Singh (Compliance), Ethan Cole (Product)

Summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
Customer evaluating Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for LLM inference; primary concerns are data residency, logging/retention, HIPAA/financial regs, encryption/KMS, and whether PII is persisted in any logs. Discussed VPC/private control plane, on-prem options, SOC2/ISO evidence, and routing/fallbacks. Agreed next steps to share security docs, schedule SE deep dive, and provide pricing for Dedicated.

Transcript:
[00:00] Ava: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we'll give people a minute. I'm Ava from Redwood, account exec. With me is Marco Ruiz, our solutions engineer.
[00:10] Lisa: Hi Ava, hi Marco. Lisa here, CISO at Bank of Riverbend. We've got Tom, Priya, Ethan on. Thanks for making time.
[00:18] Tom: Hey all.
[00:20] Marco: Thanks folks. Quick agenda, we'll do a short intro, ask about your requirements, dig into data residency, logging, and then run through deployment options — hosted, dedicated, private — and do Q&A. Sound good?
[00:32] Priya: Yep, that's what we need.
[00:35] Ethan: Fine.
[00:37] Ava: Cool. Lisa, maybe can you start with the big constraints? I know you sent a note about needing data to stay in our US region and some specific retention rules.
[00:46] Lisa: Sure. High level: Bank of Riverbend is regulated, obviously. We have customers across multiple states but want all regulated data and anything with PII to stay in the US. We also have internal policies that require admin/audit logs to be retained for 7 years in immutable storage for certain products. We need clarity on what Redwood collects, where it is stored, and control over log retention. SOC2 and ISO attestation also important.
[01:10] Marco: Understood. When you say "what Redwood collects" — are you primarily concerned about model input/outputs being stored, or the platform behavior logs like request telemetry?
[01:20] Lisa: Both. We assume model input could contain PII, so we want it either not stored, or stored only in-customer-controlled storage. And for telemetry, we need to be able to limit what's sent out.
[01:30] Tom: To add, our current architecture is GCP us-east1 for most services, some legacy on-prem data sources for sensitive records. We need to know if we can keep inference within our VPC or on-prem, and if Redwood's dedicated nodes can be in our VPC or in a private subnet.
[01:44] Marco: Yeah, we support a few deployment modes. Hosted API is our default — fast to get started — but it's multi-tenant and logs live in Redwood infrastructure. Dedicated gives you reserved capacity and isolation at the pool level; Dedicated in a cloud region can be provisioned for a single customer. Private is our customer-managed control plane — VPC peering or private endpoint options — and we also have an on-prem package for air-gapped setups.
[02:04] Priya: For Private/on-prem, does the control plane still see any PII? We need to ensure no customer data leaves the boundary.
[02:12] Marco: For Private on-prem deployments, the control plane can be configured to be customer-hosted and we can disable telemetry collection to the Redwood control plane. There may still be health metrics sent, but we can agree on minimal telemetry. I'll note that sometimes product names get jumbled in call notes — like "Redwood Privet" — but we mean private deployment.
[02:29] Lisa: (laughs) yeah.
[02:30] Ava: Real quick question on compliance — do you require HIPAA specifically, or is this more financial regs with overlap?
[02:36] Priya: It's mainly financial regs plus GLBA considerations, but we do handle a small subset of health data tied to certain benefit claims, so HIPAA-ish controls are nice to have. Basically high bar: encryption at rest, KMS/HSM, audit logs, SSO/SAML, role-based access.
[02:50] Marco: We integrate with KMS providers and can support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM integrations for Private and Dedicated setups; hosted can support KMS but keys may be in Redwood-managed KMS unless you bring your own key via a supported flow.
[03:07] Lisa: Ok, can you send us details — e.g. do you support customer-managed CMKs for hosted? That's a blocker for some teams.
[03:13] Ava: We'll include that in the security pack. Typically hosted supports BYOK for certain enterprises; I'll confirm specifics in the doc.
[03:20] [00:03:30] Tom: Can I ask about logs — what exactly is in request logs? We had a bad experience where a vendor logged full request bodies in plaintext.
[03:30] Marco: Good question. By default, our platform logs request metadata and minimal traces, but we can configure redaction. For Dedicated and Private you can disable request body retention; for Hosted, we have retention windows and a redact option. I'll be candid: Hosted has more limited controls because it's multi-tenant — we can guarantee no human review without a process, but the telemetry is in our stack.
[03:49] Priya: How about retention windows — can we set custom retention per customer?
[03:52] Marco: For Dedicated and Private, yes. Hosted has tiered retention: e.g., 30/90/365 days depending on plan and legal requirements. But Dedicated customers can set their own retention and integrate to their own S3 or equivalent for long-term audit logs, or route logs to a SIEM via our log forwarder.
[04:10] Lisa: Do you provide WORM (immutable) storage options for audit logs?
[04:13] Marco: We can integrate with S3 object lock or equivalent on the cloud provider to provide WORM for audit logs; on-prem we'd rely on your storage solution.
[04:22] Ava: Lisa, you mentioned 7 years — that's long. We'll call that out and include specific architecture patterns that meet that.
[04:29] [00:04:40] Ethan: Another networking Q — for Private, how do you handle egress and routing? Can we keep traffic within our VPC?
[04:36] Marco: With Private deployments we can either deploy the runtime into your VPC (private nodes) or provide private endpoints so traffic never traverses public internet. For Dedicated in a cloud region, we can do VPC peering or private link. There's sometimes a small control-plane management channel; in strict air-gapped mode we can remove the outbound control-plane and do local-only management.
[04:55] Tom: What about model updates and model artifacts — are they hosted by Redwood or can we host them?
[04:59] Marco: Models can be hosted in our model store; for Private/Dedicated you can bring your own model artifacts and store them in your S3 or on-prem registry. Model provenance and signing is available for critical models.
[05:12] Priya: Provenance is important. Also, we need to know about third-party libs in the runtime - any OSS licensing issues, potential vulnerabilities.
[05:19] Marco: We can supply SBOMs for the runtime images. We'll include that in the pack.
[05:23] Ava: Are there any timeline constraints from your side?
[05:26] Lisa: We'd like to decide by end of Q3. Pilot ideally in August; POC around Sep. Budget cycles.
[05:33] Ava: Ok good. Our typical pilot is 4-6 weeks.
[05:36] [00:06:00] Tom: On the technical side, latency vs cost — how predictable is per-token latency in Dedicated vs Hosted? We have SLAs for certain customer-facing flows.
[05:45] Marco: Dedicated gives more predictable latency because of reserved GPU pools. Hosted is best-effort and has autoscaling, but you can see variability depending on global load. We provide per-route SLOs for Dedicated and Private with monitoring and tracing; we can instrument the whole request with token-level latency breakdowns.
[06:03] Tom: Any fallback behavior? If we lose Dedicated capacity, do you failover to hosted?
[06:09] Marco: Yes — we support smart routing and fallbacks. We'll only do that if you enable cross-tier fallback; otherwise we fail-open with configurable behavior. We recommend canary or A/B rollout.
[06:18] Priya: Back to data residency — do you have a formal data residency guarantee for Hosted?
[06:22] Marco: For Hosted, we can restrict region (e.g., US-only), but because of multitenancy, the control plane and some telemetry may live in our global control region. For strict residency guarantees we recommend Dedicated or Private.
[06:34] Lisa: Are you SOC 2 Type II?
[06:36] Ava: Yes, we are SOC 2 Type II and have ISO 27001. We'll send the certs.
[06:41] Lisa: Good. Want to see the evidence.
[06:43] [00:06:50] Ethan: One more practical thing: our compliance team will demand a data flow diagram that shows exactly what goes where and who's able to see plain text. Can you produce example diagrams?
[06:53] Marco: Absolutely — we'll include sample data flow diagrams for Hosted/Dedicated/Private and annotate who has access to logs, where KMS keys live, etc.
[07:01] Tom: If we go Private, how much ops overhead? Our infra team is small.
[07:07] Marco: Private/on-prem has higher ops overhead. We offer an on-prem package that includes installation support and a managed services add-on if you want Redwood to operate updates. Dedicated is a middle ground — we manage the runtime but within isolated pools.
[07:20] Priya: Regarding encryption, do you support encrypting in-flight between our services and the runtime using mTLS?
[07:26] Marco: Yes, mTLS support for all private endpoints; mutual auth and client certs. We also have VPC private links.
[07:33] Lisa: We're concerned about redaction. Can Redwood redact or scrub PII automatically from inputs?
[07:39] Marco: We have a pre-processing layer where you can run PII scrubbers or tokenization before hitting the model. For Hosted, we offer optional redaction at the API layer (pattern-based). For Dedicated/Private you can host your own preprocessor. There's a feature called "prefix/KV cache" that sometimes gets called out — sorry people mispronounce KV as "KV cash" in notes — it's just the cache mechanism for tokens. Caching could store prefixes, so we recommend scrub or avoid caching sensitive prefixes.
[08:06] Tom: Good to know. How about data deletion? If we request deletion of all our data, is that immediate?
[08:12] Marco: For Hosted, we have documented deletion flows — we can purge data within a certain SLA, but backups or archived logs might have independent retention windows. For Dedicated/Private you control retention and deletion. We'll detail the deletion process in the security pack.
[08:26] [00:08:35] Priya: Any legal/contractual controls you offer around data processing agreements and data residency clauses?
[08:40] Ava: We have DPAs and can add specific residency clauses in enterprise contracts. We'll share a template.
[08:45] Lisa: Competitors? We've evaluated Anthropic and standard OpenAI enterprise. What differentiates Redwood on these controls?
[08:52] Ava: Main differentiators are unified runtime across Hosted/Dedicated/Private, clear dedicated capacity options, and built-in observability like token-level tracing and per-route cost latency breakdowns. Also our focus on deployment flexibility and enterprise controls — we can do on-prem air-gapped if required.
[09:06] Marco: In practice, some vendors don't give as granular control over logs and keys. We try to make retention and KMS explicit.
[09:12] [00:09:25] Tom: Operational question — how do upgrades happen on Dedicated? Are we impacted?
[09:30] Marco: We do rolling upgrades with canaries and can schedule maintenance windows. For Dedicated you have more control over timing; for Private on-prem you control upgrades unless you opt into managed updates.
[09:41] Priya: Any SOC2 exclusions or notable exceptions?
[09:44] Ava: We'll include the SOC2 carve-outs in the doc.
[09:46] Lisa: Regarding network logs and access — we need RBAC that integrates with our SSO (SAML/Okta).
[09:52] Marco: Supported. Our RBAC integrates with SAML and OIDC providers; we also have fine-grained role configs.
[09:58] Tom: Could you provide an example least-privilege role for ops teams that allows deployment but not access to request payloads?
[10:04] Marco: Yes, that's a common ask. We'll include role templates.
[10:08] [00:10:20] Ethan: Any limit on model sizes or seq lengths? We have some long-context requirements for certain audits.
[10:15] Marco: We support models up to long context — specifics depend on model architecture. For long context and throughput we can recommend quantized models and kernel optimizations; we'll provide performance profiles.
[10:25] Priya: Back to PHI — if we have HIPAA concerns, do you sign BAAs?
[10:29] Ava: We can sign BAAs for certain enterprise agreements and will include the legal team touchpoint.
[10:34] Lisa: Good.
[10:36] [00:10:40] Tom: For the POC, we want a small test with our redacted dataset and then a benchmark with real latency numbers. Can Redwood run a benchmark in our VPC or do we need to ship data?
[10:47] Marco: We can run benchmarks in your VPC with Private/Dedicated deployments; for Hosted we can provide representative benchmarks. Running in your VPC gives the most accurate numbers.
[10:55] Priya: If we run in our VPC, are logs still forwarded to Redwood for support?
[10:59] Marco: Only if you enable log forwarding; we can also configure long-term retention to your S3.
[11:04] Ava: Alright, I want to quickly summarize before we run out of time. Key asks: 1) Data residency / US-only; 2) KMS/BYOK options; 3) Log retention + WORM support; 4) RBAC + SSO; 5) Private/Dedicated deployment options and ops overhead; 6) SOC2/ISO evidence + SBOM. Anything to add?
[11:22] Lisa: Also sample data flows and proof of deletion.
[11:26] Tom: And latency benchmarks in our VPC for POC.
[11:29] Priya: Templates for role-based access and DPA.
[11:33] Ava: Great. Next steps we'll send security pack and pricing. Marco will schedule an SE deep dive to map network topology and the POC plan.
[11:41] Marco: I'll follow up with a calendar invite for a 60-90 minute technical deep dive. During that we'll ask for sample data flows, network diagrams, and the list of PII sources.
[11:50] Lisa: Sounds good. Any blockers on your side to get started?
[11:53] Ava: On our side we'll assemble the pack and get back on timelines. No blockers.
[11:58] Tom: Last Q — if we go Dedicated, do we get SLA credits?
[12:02] Marco: Yes, Dedicated is SLA-backed with uptime and latency SLOs per the contract. We'll include the SLA language.
[12:09] Ethan: One tiny nit: will you provide an example runbook for incident response when model outputs cause issues?
[12:15] Marco: We have runbook templates and mitigation strategies and will include them.
[12:19] [00:12:30] Ava: Ok let's do a quick recap of action items: Ava will send SOC2/ISO/KMS details and pricing, Marco will schedule SE deep dive and prepare diagrams/SBOM, Tom will share data flow diagrams and PII list. Anything else?
[12:33] Lisa: No that's it. Thanks.
[12:35] Ava: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up over email with the pack and invite.
[12:40] Lisa: Bye.
[12:41] Tom: Bye.

End of meeting.

Notes on transcription quality: speaker overlaps minimal, occasional mis-typed product names (Privet/Privated/ Dedicate instead of Dedicated), KV cache sometimes rendered as "KV cash".
